topic: #1204 plan-time grounding — plain-English goals against the local docs corpus

provenance.status: SALVAGE — partial recovery, not the original evidence
provenance.what_was_lost: The disproof validated four gates over 164 goals in four sets (design 21, held-out 50, held-out 55, held-out 38). Those goals were never written to disk — no goal file was added or deleted in the whole #1204 branch history, and none is present in the gitignored evidence directory. They existed only in the authoring session's context and its scratch probe scripts.
provenance.why_it_matters: The conclusions in the companion document cannot be reproduced, extended, or challenged without them. Worse, the loss is not repairable by effort: a held-out set cannot be re-blinded once the reader knows what broke the gates. Reconstruction yields 164 DIFFERENT goals, not these.
provenance.what_this_file_is: Every goal the companion document and ticket #1204 quote verbatim, banked before the prose is archived and they rot too. Roughly 20 of 164. It is a seed, not a replacement.
provenance.recovered_by: independent review session, 2026-07-31, before any further attempt on this defect

recording_rules.verbatim_only: Per the companion document's own rule — a measurement whose input is abbreviated is unreproducible by construction. Every string below is quoted exactly. Any goal that survives only in truncated form is marked verbatim=false and MUST NOT be cited beside a number.
recording_rules.state_the_population: A rank without its ranked population is as ambiguous as a query with an ellipsis. Where the source gave a rank, the population is recorded with it.

word_level_evidence.note: Gate 1 asked whether corpus document frequency can separate topic words from sentence scaffolding. These ten rows are the disproof: the classes interleave on the number line.

module_name_traps.note: 163 plain-lowercase words resolve to a library/<name> page and pass gates 1+2+4. These 16 were confirmed present in the passing set, and are exactly the vocabulary a non-technical operator writes.
module_name_traps.population_discrepancy: independent review reported 153; re-measurement gave 163 under the stated method (^[a-z]+$, len>=3, df ratio <=0.05, resolving to library/<name> with no fragment)

known_dead_ends.note: Six approaches are measured-and-rejected in the companion document. Read it before proposing any of these. The root cause is word-sense disambiguation, which no lexical statistic derived from the corpus can settle.
rejected: gate 1 — salience by corpus document frequency
gate 2 — require the word to resolve as a symbol
gate 4 — restrict to library/<name> module pages
candidate 5 — threshold on the corroborating page's score
candidate 6 — naming context ('use X', 'the X module')
